set.body:
Current prerequisites (replace historical dependency prose): bd-01M2WVCEBHAZBKJQ0EB84EA4HV

Scheduling lane: next. Current plan: docs/refactor/PLAN.md. Live dependency edges supersede historical sequencing below.

Operative scope 2026-09-19 (docs/refactor/PLAN.md): Foundation prerequisite of shared local evidence and the preview. Baseline capture precedes this migration; remove the old D1B prerequisite. Retain typed external/empty-eligible NotApplicable semantics and full wire migration tests. No empty eligible set may advertise fully supported.

Historical rationale and acceptance, with old dependency/fleet text superseded by live Mote edges:
Current disposition, 2026-09-19; governing docs/refactor/PLAN.md.
Retained with its original acceptance scope; recheck against current code before implementation or closure. Not a prerequisite for the annotation-assisted preview.

Original scope retained below for evidence; fleet procedure/assignments are historical and do not govern single-developer work.

supportWeight MUST NOT PUBLISH A NUMERIC CLAIM ON AN EMPTY ELIGIBLE SET. Raised independently by
collab and grok against the chief's letter; both are right and the fix is LARGER than the
eligible-set carrier I ruled for earlier.

THE DEFECT, visible in m1's own WOG ranking table:

  ext:Intrusion             total 1.0000   support 1.000   terms 0
  sit:wog:sit:lack-arrows   total 1.4806   support 0.955   terms 5

THE INTRUSION REPORTS HIGHER SUPPORT THAN THE REAL ANCHOR WHILE HAVING MEASURED NOTHING.
scaleToEligible (cost.scala:755) returns 1.0 when `eligible.isEmpty`, so `supportWeight = 1.0` means
BOTH "every eligible term was measured" AND "nothing was eligible". The field built to let a consumer
refuse a weaker claim is, on this table, ARGUING FOR THE INTRUSION.

WHY CARRYING `eligible: Set[CostTerm]` IS NECESSARY AND NOT SUFFICIENT -- this is the part I got too
small. I ruled that publishing the eligible set makes the denominator inspectable. It does. But as
grok puts it: if the external cell STILL STORES THE SAME FIELD, one wrapper over both meanings is THE
DEFECT CLASS WEARING A NEW NAME. An inspectable denominator still lets a numeric comparison run
between a cell that measured five terms and a cell for which the question does not arise.

THE ACCEPTANCE RULE, collab's sentence, adopted verbatim as the bar:
  AN EMPTY ELIGIBLE DENOMINATOR CANNOT PUBLISH THE NUMERIC CLAIM "FULLY SUPPORTED".

So external-state support is either NOT APPLICABLE to content terms, or it is its own typed evidence
contract. Not a Double that happens to be 1.0. Candidate shapes for whoever takes this:
  Support = Measured(share, eligible) | NotApplicable(reason)   -- content terms do not arise here
and a compile-level guarantee that NotApplicable cannot enter a comparison with Measured.

SEQUENCING, from grok and not negotiable: SUPPORT HONESTY LANDS BEFORE ANYONE FITS THE FLOOR. A
calibration run whose support column conflates two meanings will fit the constant against a number
that is partly fiction. This bead is UPSTREAM of calibration even though calibration is the headline.

DEPENDS ON: nothing external -- executable NOW. Touches CostBreakdown, so it sequences behind the
align candidates currently in flight (bd-01M16M5ETH0QHFZ62KXZJ54PN9) and shares a boundary with
sweep 3 slice one, which wants CostBreakdown unforgeable anyway. Doing both in one candidate is
worth considering.
BLOCKS: the calibration claim, and any published support comparison.
set.title: G1: honest support assessment before shared evidence and confidence
